comparator.name: Digital Society
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 regulations and faculty outline confirm the English full-time Digital Society BA. Years one and two each contain 60 EC of required study. Year three contains 30 EC of approved electives, 4 EC of research experimentation, 9 EC of controversies and a 17 EC thesis. The third-year mentoring scheme is optional and carries no credits. The electives remain genuine choice space. Progression and assessment follow the regulations.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum has twelve courses in programming, computer science, AI, data science and mathematics (Introduction to Programming, Mathematical Methods, Introduction to Data Science, Machine Learning, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, AI Ethics, Decision-making in AI, Optimization Methods in AI, Networks & Operating Systems, Database Management Systems, Algorithms & Data Structures and Probability & Statistics), three on research methods and statistics (Research Methods & Statistics, Statistics & Experimental Methods and Qualitative Research Methodology), and eight on the social, ethical and behavioural side (Ethics, Human Rights, Persuasive Communication, From T.V. to TikTok, Media Archaeology, Calling Bullshit, Marketing & Consumer Engagement and Behavioral Economics), plus Personal & Professional Development. The label names the technical majority first and the social and behavioural perspectives second; it does not claim a full computer-science or data-science degree.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: This option uses 8 different courses to deepen networks, databases, mathematical statistics, AI decision-making and neural networks, and add behavioural economics and digital marketing. The first option devotes more courses to sociology, media interpretation, public policy, creative practice and the social impacts of AI.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Introductory media and sociology precede advanced study of media narratives and publics. Research Methods & Statistics precedes Statistics & Experimental Methods, and data handling precedes Machine Learning. Programming precedes advanced algorithms and optimisation.

basisLabels: Digital cultures, media and the history of ICT: Digital Cultures, Virtual Worlds and ICT Revolutions: Continuity and Change, covering influencers, virtual worlds, emerging media and the historical development of computing
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Film & Media introduces the study of film and media, tracing the historical development of cinema and the elements of film form (narrative, cinematography, editing, sound) and treating media as cultural forms that reflect and shape society; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the target's media and digital-culture analysis by supplying the analytical vocabulary, although its main object is film rather than digital media. It implements the explicit academic basis “Digital cultures, media and the history of ICT: Digital Cultures, Virtual Worlds and ICT Revolutions: Continuity and Change, covering influencers, virtual worlds, emerging media and the historical development of computing”.

basisLabels: Digital cultures, media and the history of ICT: Digital Cultures, Virtual Worlds and ICT Revolutions: Continuity and Change, covering influencers, virtual worlds, emerging media and the historical development of computing
courseTraceability.rationale: Media Archaeology studies how pre-digital media technologies such as cassette tapes, typewriters and printed books shaped the production, circulation and preservation of knowledge, through material analysis and historical interpretation; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the target's history-of-ICT component (ICT Revolutions: Continuity and Change) but addresses earlier media technologies rather than the digital revolution itself. It implements the explicit academic basis “Digital cultures, media and the history of ICT: Digital Cultures, Virtual Worlds and ICT Revolutions: Continuity and Change, covering influencers, virtual worlds, emerging media and the historical development of computing”.

basisLabels: Digital technologies and critical making: Introduction to Digital Technologies I and II, Critical Making, the basics of coding and cyber security, and designing digital systems for social good
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Programming teaches structured and object-oriented programming in Python with testing and debugging; it offers a partial contribution to the basics of coding that the programme page names for the target's Introduction to Digital Technologies I, although it is a computer-science gateway course rather than a digital-society course. It implements the explicit academic basis “Digital technologies and critical making: Introduction to Digital Technologies I and II, Critical Making, the basics of coding and cyber security, and designing digital systems for social good”.

basisLabels: Digital society as an interdisciplinary object of study: how digitalisation transforms culture, politics, the economy and the environment, introduced in What is (a) Digital Society?, Artificial Society and Controversies in Digital Society

It implements the explicit academic basis “Digital society as an interdisciplinary object of study: how digitalisation transforms culture, politics, the economy and the environment, introduced in What is (a) Digital Society?, Artificial Society and Controversies in Digital Society”.

notes.text: UCR offers substantial work in AI, data, media and social analysis. Maastricht integrates these areas through dedicated study of digital politics and regulation, virtual worlds and critical making. UCR’s creative laboratory includes experimental forms, with digital media as one part of that work.

Maastricht requires 120 EC in the first two years. Year three includes 30 EC of approved electives, 4 EC of research experimentation, 9 EC of controversies and a 17 EC individual thesis. UCR’s optional independent research sits outside the displayed 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: Maastricht Digital Society studies how digital technologies shape culture, politics, organisations and everyday life. It combines humanities and social-science analysis with digital skills, data, ethical inquiry and interdisciplinary research. The final year includes approved electives, research experimentation, controversies and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR option combines media and social analysis with computing, AI and policy. The second focuses on the technical workings of data and AI while examining their social effects. Maastricht brings these areas together in dedicated digital society courses and requires a 17 EC individual thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC includes 120 EC of compulsory study in the first two years. Year three combines 30 EC of approved electives with research experimentation, controversies and a thesis.
